attachments.name: medical_plan.txt
attachments.text:
EVENT MEDICAL PLAN
PHU Athletics Founders Race 10K, Sunday 21 November 2027
Applicant: Port Halden University Athletics
Issue: 3.4

1. Event summary
A 10K race with 60 runners, starting at 10:00 in the Eastfield area of Port Halden. An ambulance from Sentinel Ambulance Service is on site for the race; the paperwork is attached.

Runners get an email in race week telling them to dress for the weather and to keep a phone with them if they can. Most have run with us before. The list of entrants includes an emergency contact for each runner, which is kept at the start.

2. First aid cover
3 first aid posts will operate, at the start, at the finish and at the course midpoint, staffed by 6 qualified first aiders. Posts are placed so that no part of the course is more than 1.5 km from one. Two cycle responders move along the course with defibrillators.

3. Weather and hydration
Water is available every 2.5 km. The race director checks the forecast 48 hours and 2 hours before the start. Above 28 degrees C the start is brought forward or the course shortened, and above 32 degrees C the race is cancelled. In cold or wet conditions, foil blankets and a warm shelter are at the finish.

4. Transfer to hospital
The receiving hospital is Northshore District Hospital, 11 km from the finish. The transfer route and the pick-up point at the top of Linden Avenue have been walked with the first aid team. The hospital's emergency department has been told the date and the expected numbers.

5. Communications
Every first aid post and cycle responder carries a radio on the medical channel, with phones as backup. All calls for an ambulance go through the medical lead, who gives the crew the access point and the nearest barrier to open.

6. Clinical lead
The medical lead is Joan Kowalczyk, a registered paramedic, who is on site from an hour before the start until the last runner is cleared. The lead can have any runner withdrawn on medical grounds.

attachments.name: race_plan.txt
attachments.text:
PHU Athletics Founders Race 10K: how the race will work

Prepared by Lucas Ferreira (Volunteer Coordinator), Port Halden University Athletics. Last updated 14 July 2027.

This is our plan for race day, Sunday 21 November 2027. We expect 60 runners over 10K (10 km). Numbers can be collected from the top of Linden Avenue from an hour before we go at 10:00, and we aim to have the last finisher home by 12:00.

The route takes in Linden Avenue, Fenwick Street and Albion Road, and the City would need to close all of these for us. On the way round we cross Cross Avenue and Victoria Road. We finish in Ferry Park lawn.

These are all big, wide streets. We measured Linden Avenue at 16 metres and Albion Road at 10 metres, kerb to kerb, not counting the pavements. People watching have the pavement and the grass strip to spread out on.

Our club has put on races for some years now and we keep to the same simple format: chip timing, water on the course, and a hot drink at the end. Results go up on our website the same evening.

attachments.name: traffic_plan.txt
attachments.text:
TRAFFIC MANAGEMENT PLAN
Event: PHU Athletics Founders Race 10K
Date: Sunday 21 November 2027
Applicant: Port Halden University Athletics
Prepared by: Corvus Temporary Works
Issue: 3.4

1. Scope
This plan describes how traffic will be managed for the PHU Athletics Founders Race 10K, a 10K race in the Eastfield area of Port Halden with a 10:00 start. It has been prepared to accompany the permit application and should be read with the race plan. Police attendance is covered in the attached correspondence.

2. Road closures
Temporary closures will be in force as follows, with barriers and advance signing supplied by Northline Barriers.
- Linden Avenue, Bell Street to Rope Walk: closed 08:45 to 12:30
- Fenwick Street, Bell Street to Glebe Road: closed 08:45 to 12:30
- Albion Road, Ash Avenue to Glebe Road: closed 08:45 to 12:30

We have a good working relationship with local residents. Several members walk the route the week before, noting anything that has changed, such as new roadworks, a barrier left in place, or a lane marked for cycles.

3. Major crossings
Each major crossing has its own control point, staffed from 08:45 until the last runner has passed.
- Cross Avenue at Linden Avenue: 3 traffic marshals with stop/go boards, one supervisor
- Victoria Road at Linden Avenue: 4 traffic marshals with stop/go boards, one supervisor

4. Diversions
Signed diversions will operate for the duration of the closures.
- Linden Avenue: traffic diverted via Station Road and Queen's Road, signed from Rope Walk
- Fenwick Street: traffic diverted via Regent Road and Tram Street, signed from Ash Avenue
- Albion Road: traffic diverted via Prince Street and High Street, signed from Bell Street

5. Emergency vehicle access
A clear lane of at least 3.5 m will be kept along the closed section for emergency vehicles. Barrier staff hold radios on the event channel and can open any closure within two minutes on request from the event controller, who is in direct contact with the police and ambulance control rooms.

6. Notification
Details of the event will be published on the organiser's website and shared through social media in the weeks leading up to race day.

7. Reopening
A sweep vehicle follows the last runner. Closures are lifted in the order listed, after a barrier and litter check, with all roads open by 12:30.
